column1: # INEGI ENIGH 2024 gastos (COICOP 2018 / CCIF 2018) code prefix → aisle. Human file (drafted by the research on 2026-10-21,
# revised by Claude (AI) on 2026-10-22; awaiting owner review). The longest matching prefix wins; "-" = skip; codes that
# match no prefix are skipped (services, clothing, transport...).

column3: food and non-alcoholic drinks not listed below: pantry
cookies sit in abarrotes (QQP: Galletas Pastas y Harinas de Trigo)
tostadas are sold at the tortillería
game meats (horse, iguana, frog, turtle, venison): not supermarket items
ham, bacon, smoked and dried meat, cold cuts
carne adobada o enchilada is raw marinated meat at the meat counter
milk, cheese, yoghurt, eggs ("Lácteos y huevo")
dulces de leche and jamoncillos are sweets (QQP's Cajeta is mapped to abarrotes, which wins)
margarine sits with butter in the refrigerated case
chicharrón (pork rind) is sold at the meat counter (store-dependent: bagged chicharrones are snacks)
dried fruit sits with nuts and snacks
ready-made gelatin cups are in the refrigerated dairy case (store-dependent)
protein powder and supplements sit with pharmacy goods (QQP lists Suplemento Alimenticio under Medicamentos)
light bulbs (ENIGH household accessories), sold with household goods
batteries (ENIGH household accessories), sold with household goods
adult incontinence products sit with personal care (as QQP's Ropa Interior Desechable)

column1: # ENIGH's "18" block (181113-181171) names extra household food items one code at a time (no COICOP tree under it),
# so each useful code is mapped by itself; codes left out are generic ("Otras especias"), services, gifts, or labels whose
# pieces would read wrong ("Plátano verde y Tabasco" would make "tabasco" a fruit; "Anís (licor)" would make anís a drink).
# Added by the auditor (Claude, AI) on 2026-10-22.

filete de pescado (fresh fish counter; breaded or frozen fillets are 011331)
fish and roe: anguilas, mantarraya, pejelagarto, hueva de pescado
aguamiel, pulque, tepache and other fermented drinks
aceite de coco, aceite de soya (cooking oils)
pápalo, flor de calabaza, chaya (fresh greens)
harina para waffles o hot cakes (as QQP's Harina Hot Cakes)
